documentation.range: This species is endemic to Chile and occurs on the western slope of the Andes between Vallenar and Curico, from sea level to 1,800 m (Vertzi et al. 2015).
documentation.population: This is an abundant species and one of the most well-known of the small mammals in Chile (Ojeda pers. comm., Verzi et al. 2015).
documentation.habitats: This species inhabits semi-arid environments on the Western Slope of the Andes, often found in open areas near rocks (Verzi et al. 2015). They usually have four to six offspring in the spring and summer (September-October, December-January).
documentation.threats: There are no major threats for this species at present.
documentation.measures: There are no specific conservation measures in place to protect this rodent.
documentation.rationale: This species is listed as Least Concern in view of its relatively wide distribution, presumed large population, and because it is unlikely to be declining at nearly the rate required to qualify for listing in a threatened category.
